Definition: from G4862 and G3140; to testify jointly, i.e. corroborate by (concurrent) evidence:--testify unto, (also) bear witness (with).
BiblicalUsage: The Spirit Himself bears witness with our spirit that we are the children of God, so assurance is not a voice inside my head alone but God's Spirit agreeing with mine. Paul says the conscience also bears witness, with thoughts accusing or excusing, and in Romans 9 he calls his conscience to bear him witness in the Holy Ghost that his sorrow for Israel is real.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God gives His children a double witness, His Spirit with my spirit and a conscience kept clean before Him. I hold that this is how assurance works: not by my feelings alone, but by the Spirit agreeing with a conscience that tells the truth.
